paragraphs.text: This is Lake Powell in July 2019. Now the same bays in September 2026.
Lake Powell and Lake Mead together held 74 percent less water in September 2026 than at the start of 2000.

stat.label: less water in Lake Powell and Lake Mead than in January 2000
stat.note: 46.5 million acre-feet then, 12.0 million on 16 September 2026
stat.source: Bureau of Reclamation daily data; our calculation

paragraphs.text: Reclamation saw it coming. In March 2024 its engineers set out how they would run Glen Canyon Dam if the lake kept falling.

document.highlight: Establishment of Interim Operating Guidance for Glen Canyon Dam during Low Reservoir Levels at Lake Powell
document.title: Technical Decision Memorandum, 26 March 2024

paragraphs.text: Downstream, Hoover Dam went up in the 1930s, built for a fuller river.
From Lake Havasu, the Central Arizona Project pumps water to Phoenix and Tucson. The Colorado River Aqueduct carries it west toward Los Angeles.
Even the four upper states call the new rules a stopgap. So who should give up water first?

document.text: Today's framework does not represent a final solution.
